hero.title: Lab
hero.description: Quantitative finance demos that run in your browser. Move the parameters and see what happens to the price distribution, the efficient frontier or a pair's z-score.
hero.tech: Plain JavaScript · no server · no login
hero.disclaimer: Educational content, not investment advice. The simulations use simplified models and parameters you choose; past or simulated results do not guarantee future results.

demos.title: Demos
demos.intro: Each demo has a short explanation, the main parameters and the code behind it. Where there is one, I link the full project with real data.

monteCarlo.title: Monte Carlo price paths
monteCarlo.description: Simulates thousands of paths with geometric Brownian motion and shows the fan of possible outcomes.

frontier.title: Efficient frontier
frontier.description: Build a portfolio with 2 to 4 assets, tune returns, vols and correlations and watch the Markowitz frontier move.

pairs.title: Pairs z-score
pairs.description: Generate two cointegrated prices, pick the window and entry bands and see when the spread drifts away and comes back.

kelly.title: Kelly and position sizing
kelly.description: Compare Kelly fractions on a repeated bet and see the effect on growth, drawdown and risk of ruin.

blackScholes.title: Black-Scholes and the Greeks
blackScholes.description: Price of a European option and its Greeks as a function of the underlying price, time to expiry and implied volatility.

real.description: The demos use synthetic data. To see the same ideas applied to real assets, the full projects:

mc.title: Monte Carlo price paths
mc.intro: Geometric Brownian motion: each day's log return is normal, with constant mean and volatility. It is the model behind Black-Scholes, and also its biggest simplification.
mc.sigmaHint: annualized standard deviation of log returns
mc.paramsNote: Illustrative parameters chosen by you, not estimated from any asset. Educational content, not investment advice.
mc.fanAria: Fan of {{n}} simulated paths over {{days}} trading days, starting at {{s0}}. Final median {{median}}, P5 to P95 range from {{p5}} to {{p95}}.
mc.histAria: Final price histogram: {{below}} of the paths end below S₀ ({{s0}}). Median {{median}}.
mc.obsPositive: With σ = {{sigma}}, the mean ({{mean}}) sits above the median ({{median}}): a few very high paths pull the mean up. In {{below}} of the simulations the price ends below S₀, even with a positive drift. Raise the vol to watch the fan widen and the skew grow.
mc.obsNegative: With σ = {{sigma}}, the mean ({{mean}}) sits above the median ({{median}}): a few very high paths pull the mean up. With a negative drift, {{below}} of the simulations end below S₀. Raise the vol to watch the fan widen and the skew grow.
mc.obsDrag: Notice: μ is positive but μ − σ²/2 is negative. The typical path (median) falls even with a positive average return; that is “volatility drag”.
mc.formulaText: Z ~ N(0,1), drawn with Box-Muller; Δt = 1/252. The −σ²/2 term makes the median grow at μ − σ²/2 per year, while the mean grows at μ. The higher the vol, the bigger the gap between them.
mc.memory: The simulation steps day by day with a vector of N prices and only computes percentiles on the days that are charted, so it never stores the full path matrix. It runs in a Web Worker so the page stays responsive.

1.title: 01 · In the browser
1.text: Each demo is a module loaded only when you reach it. Nothing runs on a server; the site stays static on GitHub Pages.

2.title: 02 · Open source
2.text: The “Show code” button shows the formula and the JavaScript snippet that draws the chart. The same code is in the repository.
